per_claim_review.title: Profinite quotients and finite coordinates.
per_claim_review.finding: The non-Hausdorff starting convention is handled: compact total disconnectedness makes singleton closures trivial and hence the group Hausdorff. The quasi-component/clopen argument, finite-index stabilizer, normal-core construction, closed-subgroup separation and quotient inverse-limit reconstruction are complete.

per_claim_review.title: The relative pro-\(\ell\) residual, with its exact ambient meaning.
per_claim_review.finding: The original ambient open-normal PL intersection is identified with the intrinsic pro-ell residual using finite intersections and normal cores. The finite-quotient criterion and the noncommutative product-one tuple proof of Cauchy are sufficient; no arithmetic pro-ell descent is assumed here.

per_claim_review.title: Functoriality and surjective images of the relative residual.
per_claim_review.finding: The continuous-map inclusion really permits an arbitrary target subgroup H-prime. Equality is confined to the printed surjective/full-preimage/open-normal setting and follows from the compact quotient criterion. This matches original pl_map and does not silently require target normality in the inclusion-only lemma.

per_claim_review.title: Finite \(\ell\)-groups are detected by linear characters.
per_claim_review.finding: The finite ell-group normalizer argument makes a maximal proper subgroup normal of index ell. The resulting F_ell character separates it, including ell=2. The proof does not use the desired finite-generation statement circularly.

per_claim_review.title: The exact finite-character generator bound.
per_claim_review.finding: Finite HomL is a finite F_ell vector space. An evaluation basis supplies generators, and a proper closed generated subgroup would be detected in a finite quotient by LIM4. Padding uses d <= ell^d = |HomL| <= b, which is exactly strong enough for the source fin0/finN bound.

per_claim_review.title: A single finitely generated quotient for every local map.
per_claim_review.finding: One fixed quotient Y/PL(f0 inverse H) works for every original local map. PhiCond is used on that exact open subgroup and its required open subgroups, and original ProL kills the residual simultaneously. This is a uniform factorization, not a different finitely generated quotient for each level.

per_claim_review.title: A free profinite group on a prescribed finite list.
per_claim_review.finding: The construction from the product of all finite quotients of the free word group includes an explicit compactness argument and the full continuous universal property. Compatible finite-coordinate maps recover maps to arbitrary profinite targets. The empty-generator case is included.

per_claim_review.title: One finite profinite cover for all original levels.
per_claim_review.finding: The one finite free profinite cover sends its distinguished generator to the original c_N, uses the same quotient coset representatives at all levels, and pads the original hb-generated H_N. The maps are surjective and their reductions modulo H agree on a dense generating subgroup. Involution is deferred correctly to the later quotient.

per_claim_review.title: One ultrafilter and exact stabilization of the kernel joins.
per_claim_review.finding: One ultrafilter extending the tail filter stabilizes whole finite-quotient kernel images. Compactness proves K V equals the stabilized finite subgroup for every open normal V. This establishes exact kernel-join equality without interchanging an infinite intersection with eventuality.

per_claim_review.title: Uniform convergence of the outgoing homomorphisms.
per_claim_review.finding: Finite topological generation makes the set of entire continuous homomorphisms into each finite quotient finite. Whole-map stabilization is compatible across quotients and produces a continuous surjection F. The common K is killed, giving the original uniform outgoing comparison.

per_claim_review.finding: The actual quotient G-star=Pi/K, its quotient map and h-star are constructed on the same cover. The all-level comparison modulo H is stronger than eventual convergence because the free generators were chosen with the same quotient images.

per_claim_review.title: Uniform finite local homomorphisms.
per_claim_review.finding: After eventual kernel-join equality, each finite incoming map factors through the same finitely generated local quotient from LIM6. Stabilizing these entire finite homomorphisms gives uniformity over every local element. Finite compatibility checks are performed before passage to the inverse limit.

per_claim_review.finding: The inverse-limit local map is continuous and has the exact original Close orientation x inverse x-prime in V. The replacement of a lift by xk resolves the K V ambiguity. The equality h-star F_Y=f0 follows in every finite base quotient, uniformly in the local element.

per_claim_review.finding: Both original finite families Vl and St are treated, with the actual phi and phiU maps and their separate PhiCond fields. Finite intersections yield one eventual set for all places and all local elements, preserving the original kernel codomains, Iv and Ju.

per_claim_review.finding: The limit Frobenius and tame elements arise from lifts of the actual ph_N and ta_N in the same Pi and the same ultrafilter. per_claim_review.finding: The original tame relation is evaluated in each fixed finite ell-quotient. The ell-power order exponent is bounded by the finite quotient size, so the tail Nq congruence forces commutation there. Passing through every K V proves exact commutation in the limit; tame elements are not claimed trivial.
